correctness.rationale: Fourier differentiation gives the STFT as -i times a nonzero phase times W=(A+B)cos(theta)+i(A-B)sin(theta), with theta=pi Delta t and A,B the shifted odd Gaussians. They cannot vanish together. The same-sign and opposite-sign regions therefore force t=T/2 and 0, respectively, modulo T. No zero lies at nu=+-d; on nu=0 the zero set has exactly the time spacing T, proving the fundamental period. The ratio artanh(u)/u strictly increases from 1 to infinity, while the exterior log ratio minus 4 pi d nu strictly decreases from infinity to minus infinity. This proves completeness and puts equality in the three-zero regime. The Jacobian at t=0 is -pi Delta (A-B)(A+B)' and at T/2 is -pi Delta (A+B)(A-B)'. Differentiating the modulus ratios at the roots gives the stated nonzero signs; the derivative of artanh(u)/u is strictly positive for u>0. The critical derivative of order three of A+B is 8 pi exp(-1/2), checked independently by symbolic differentiation. The imaginary time derivative is negative after identifying its imaginary component; the oriented coordinate change (t,nu)->(nu, Im W) has positive determinant there. In these coordinates the transverse real map has a positive cubic leading term, hence degree +1. Expanding artanh(u)/u gives u^2=3 epsilon+O(epsilon^2). The signed totals agree on both sides and at equality. Replay via the two scalar equations and local derivatives in RESULT.md lines 35–85. The finite numerical checker was read, not run; exact zeros/charges are specific to the stated real gap, tones, window and (t,nu) orientation.

evidence: Set mu=4 pi d nu, alpha^2=2 pi d^2 and A=1 in the Appendix A derivative. After dividing away the nonzero amplitude factor, the equation is mu/(2 alpha^2)=sinh(mu)/(cosh(mu)+gamma). For gamma=1 this is u=tanh(alpha^2 u); for gamma=-1 and mu nonzero it is u=coth(alpha^2 u), with u=nu/d. These are exactly the frozen two root equations.

The constructive slice derivative changes from the central maximum to a minimum between two maxima. With A-B<0 this gives the central charge flip and positive side charges, using the real-slice derivative. On the destructive slice the derivative equation has simple roots off the origin because coth is strictly decreasing there; the exterior extrema are maxima of the squared difference, giving negative STFT charges on both sides. The nonzero imaginary time derivative at the central zero and tanh x=x-x^3/3+O(x^5) give the cubic degree and square-root opening without an additional spectral theorem.

evidence: Write the demodulated Gaussian transform as W_0=P exp(i theta)+Q exp(-i theta), where P,Q are the two shifted Gaussians. Then -partial_nu W_0/(2 pi) is the reduced first-Hermite transform. At the two real relative phases gamma=cos(2 theta)=1,-1, one may remove a constant phase. The derivative of the spectrogram |W_0|^2 vanishes exactly when this real amplitude or its frequency derivative vanishes.

At gamma=1 the amplitude is positive; at gamma=-1 its only zero is nu=0, and its derivative there is nonzero. Accordingly the older exact one-or-three constructive extremum count and three destructive extrema give exactly the frozen one-or-three interior and two exterior zeros; the two-slice restriction itself follows immediately from the signs of the two shifted first derivatives.

originality.rationale: The frozen classification is mechanically recoverable from the earlier exact pure-tone Gaussian spectrogram extremum analysis of Meignen–Laurent–Oberlin (2022), especially Appendix A, not merely from an older qualitative ridge heuristic. Apply its two analyzed phase slices with A=1 and sigma=1. After removing the frequency-dependent time phase, minus the frequency derivative of the Gaussian-window transform divided by 2 pi is the first-Hermite reduced transform (up to constant gauge). At the constructive slice all Gaussian spectrogram extrema correspond to first-Hermite zeros. At the destructive slice the stationary central Gaussian zero is extraneous, leaving precisely the two noncentral extrema. The paper's exact derivative equation at the two slices gives the interior and exterior root equations directly, and differentiation and the first nonconstant Taylor term of the same scalar equations give the local indices, cubic contact and splitting. The later Resultary cusp theorem also explicitly specializes to the entire frozen geometry, but its later date is not evidence of prior coverage. The failure is based on the 2022 equations and results, not on failure to retrieve a different paper.
